title: micro traffic windows and region diversion notes
content:
Notes to self: micro-traffic windows + region diversion experiment ideas (scratchpad).

Goal: reduce blast radius for model variant rollouts by combining very small initial windows, short temporal 'safety fences', and opportunistic region diversion when anomalies surface. Keep things cheap and reversible.

High-level approach (informal):
- Phase 0 (canary-lite): 0.05% global for 10m, validate basic correctness and end-to-end path.
- Phase 1 (micro-window): 0.5% for 30m, watch p50/p95 latency and token error rate.
- Phase 2 (scaled micro): 2% for 1h, selective region expansion (+EU only or +us-west).
- Phase 3 (broader): 15% for 3h, observe quality metrics (eval prompts), economics.

Region diversion idea: if a region's p99 latency increases > 30% vs baseline or error_rate > 0.75% for 5m, automatically divert that region's traffic to fallback model pool in nearest region. Fallbacks: lower-capacity quantized variant or older stable model pinned.

Safety window concepts:
- Safety fence 1 (behavioral): simple semantic checks on outputs for high-risk routes (sensitive PII redaction, hallucination heuristics). If > 2 failures in 1000 requests, pause rollout for that route.
- Safety fence 2 (telemetry): streaming anomaly detector on latency, p99, and request error spikes. If triggered, immediate diversion.
- Safety fence 3 (business): revenue-impacting errors (failed billable conversions) -> manual paging.

Metrics to watch (minimal telemetry):
- infra: p50/p95/p99 latency, gpu_util, queue_depth
- reliability: request_error_rate, model_timeouts, rate-limited responses
- quality: eval set success %, sampling of model outputs (manual review), rerank delta where relevant
- cost: cost_per_1k_tokens, token_multiplier for long sequences

Rollback / kill triggers (fast path):
- absolute: request_error_rate > 2% sustained for 10m OR p99 latency > baseline * 2 for 10m
- relative: quality regression on eval_set > 3 percentage points vs baseline AND correlated customer complaints > 1/min
- manual: SRE or release owner can hit 'drain-and-pin' button to stop rollout and pin stable model.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- create experiment in console with notes + expected metrics
- attach eval prompt set and quick smoke tests (smoke run ID)
- set telemetry hooks (alerts + slack) and ensure on-call knows window
- mark routing policy with fallback variants + region diversion enabled
- pre-warm cache where possible (prefix cache warmers)

During rollout:
- watch dashboard: first 15m tight monitoring (1m granularity)
- sample 10 outputs/min for manual QA during phase 0/1
- confirm fallback works by inducing small simulated failure in staging (dry-run)

Post-mortem notes (if rollback):
- capture full request traces for first 30m after degradation
- diff outputs vs baseline on flagged prompts
- record decision timeline: who paged, when diversion triggered, time to recover

Open questions / to-do:
- how to automate "region-specific" eval sets? cheap heuristic vs curated?
- should we allow progressive ramp without manual approval up to 20%? probably require manual at 5%->15%
- decide default timeboxes for each micro-window (10m/30m/1h/3h?)
- define sampling policy for QA (random vs stratified by route)

Quick TODOs for next run:
- add one-liner in experiment description to flag "sensitive routes" (so safety fences are route-aware)
- pair with Maya for a simulated region diversion test next Tue
- create a Confluence stub that lists the exact alert thresholds and runbook links

Random notes (voice-of-author):
- keep the first window embarrassingly small. humans often overestimate model stability.
- prefer diversion over immediate full rollback when degradation is regional or infra-correlated.

End of scratchpad.

——
Personal reminder: migrate this to a proper release template after 2 successful runs.
